news.headline: US Fed Hikes 25 bps to 3.75-4%; Warsh Signals More Hikes Possible
news.what_happened: The US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 bps to 3.75-4% on Sept 16, marking the first hike in 3 years. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said another hike in 2026 remains on the table as inflation pressures persist. Dow Jones fell 631 pts (-1.21%) on the decision.
news.why_it_matters: Fed rate hikes strengthen USD and raise US yields (10Y now at 5.006%), triggering FII outflows from emerging markets including India. Rate-sensitive sectors (banks, NBFCs, real estate) face dual pressure from higher global yields and potential RBI tightening follow-through. GIFT Nifty at 23,159 implies ~1% gap-down open.

news.headline: RBI Launches ₹1 Trillion OMO Bond Sale to Drain Surplus Liquidity
news.what_happened: RBI started its ₹50,000 Cr open market operation (OMO) bond sale today to absorb excess liquidity. Two more tranches (₹25,000 Cr each) are scheduled Sept 21 and Sept 28, completing a ₹1 trillion total drain. Banking system surplus had hit ₹11 trillion after a massive USD-INR swap facility closed Aug 31.
news.why_it_matters: Liquidity drain tightens domestic monetary conditions even without a repo rate change. Rising bond yields hurt bank bond portfolios (mark-to-market losses). NBFCs face higher borrowing costs. Real estate and auto loans become costlier, dampening demand.

news.headline: FII Net Sellers ₹2,032 Cr; DII Counter-Buys ₹3,908 Cr (Sept 16)
news.what_happened: Foreign institutional investors sold a net ₹2,032.60 Cr in Indian equities on September 16. Domestic institutional investors, led by LIC and mutual funds, bought a net ₹3,908.20 Cr, strongly cushioning the selling pressure.
news.why_it_matters: FII selling is expected to continue in the near term given the Fed hike and rising US yields. DII buying at ₹3,908 Cr is a strong buffer and supports large-cap domestic-facing stocks. Mid-caps and small-caps typically bear the brunt of FII selling.

news.headline: Tata Sons Board Meeting Today — NBFC Status, Succession & Trust Row in Focus
news.what_happened: Tata Sons is holding a critical board meeting in Mumbai on Sept 17. Three agenda items: (1) RBI ruling on Tata Sons' NBFC status, (2) Chandrasekaran succession planning, (3) Tata Trusts governance row.
news.why_it_matters: NBFC classification could restrict Tata Sons from paying large dividends/buybacks to holding entities, impacting TCS's capital return story. Management succession uncertainty could weigh on TCS and TATACONSUMER sentiment. Tata group stocks may see elevated volatility today.

news.headline: India Merchandise Exports Surge 26.12% YoY to $43.81 Bn in August
news.what_happened: India's merchandise exports hit $43.81 billion in August 2026, a 26.12% jump year-on-year, with the trade deficit narrowing. India-New Zealand FTA coming into force next month. India-China bilateral trade talks have commenced.
news.why_it_matters: Strong export data boosts pharma, IT, and textile exporters. USD/INR stability at 95.94 supports export sector earnings visibility. This is a positive macro signal for India's current account deficit trajectory.

picks.catalyst: Fed rate hike triggers global risk-off → defensive sector rotation into pharma; India August exports +26% YoY supports pharma earnings
picks.logic: Sun Pharma is India's largest pharma company with diversified US generics + branded domestic business. In risk-off sessions driven by macro shocks (not company-specific), pharma defensives attract DII buying and rotation away from banks/real estate. USD/INR flat at 95.94 keeps US earnings translation stable. FII selling hits cyclicals first; pharma holds relatively better. Reference close: ₹1,853.5.

picks.catalyst: Risk-off environment + strong DII buying ₹3,908 Cr — FMCG defensive sees rotation; crude -0.23% marginally improves packaging cost outlook
picks.logic: Hindustan Unilever is the benchmark defensive FMCG stock. In sessions where the Nifty gaps down on global macro shocks (Fed hike), HINDUNILVR typically outperforms as institutional money rotates to defensives. DII funds actively support large-cap consumer names. Crude oil slightly lower improves packaging material costs at the margin. Reference close: ₹1,962.
